answer: Bind every agent seat to a proof-of-replication pledge: at registration the agent slowly seals a unique encoded replica into dedicated physical storage, then each epoch must echo back a proof only the holder of that exact sealed sector can generate. A clone shares no disk, so its challenge returns empty and its seat lapses. Each sealed copy is bound to its own bytes like a violet pressed into one page, so a thousand claimed agents is a fable unless a thousand disks are truly sealed and occupied. The deterrent is non-amortizable physical space plus slow sequential sealing, scarce real hardware.
